metadata.note: Follow-up to syracuse_northern_railroad.geojson: in 1885, financier George Potts revived part of that railroad's abandoned Syracuse-Woodard's trackage as the start of a new route to Oswego, organized as the Syracuse, Phoenix and Oswego Railway and operated from the start as a branch of the Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg Railroad's St. Lawrence Division -- the 'Hojack' nickname (see hojack_line.geojson for the other half of that nickname's territory, Oswego west to Lewiston). Reached Phoenix by July 8 1885; 17 new miles of track continued to Fulton; trackage rights over the New York, Ontario and Western Railway completed the connection Fulton-Oswego, giving a new 37-mile Syracuse-Oswego route operational by early 1886, with five daily passenger trains each way and seasonal resort traffic to Three River Point. Leased to the New York Central along with the rest of the RW&O system in 1891. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap for Syracuse-Woodard's, Phoenix-Fulton, and Fulton-Oswego; the short Woodard's-Phoenix stretch is a straight-line approximation -- the only real track OSM offered for that stretch backtracked north past Fulton's own longitude before looping back to Phoenix, an implausible detour rejected in favor of the honest straight line.
sources: Grokipedia 'Syracuse Northern Railroad' article (see syracuse_northern_railroad.geojson sources): 1885 revival by George Potts, extension to Phoenix July 8 1885, operating as the 'Hojack' branch of the RW&O's St. Lawrence Division as the Syracuse, Phoenix and Oswego Railway; repurposed Woodard's-Syracuse trackage plus 17 new miles Woodard's-Fulton; NY,O&W trackage rights Fulton-Oswego; new 37-mile Syracuse-Oswego route operational by early 1886; five daily passenger trains each direction; Three River Point resort traffic; whole RW&O system leased to New York Central March 14 1891
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Northern_Railroad (background on the original Syracuse Northern trackage this route reused)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, overpass.openstreetmap.fr mirror): railway=rail (active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging, Syracuse to Oswego via Woodard's, Phoenix, and Fulton; routed via Dijkstra shortest path between each station's geocoded coordinates. Syracuse-Woodard's, Phoenix-Fulton, and Fulton-Oswego resolved to plausible real paths. The Woodard's-Phoenix hop's only candidate path was an implausible backtracking detour and was replaced with a straight-line fallback instead.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable outside the sourced 1886-era five-trips/day detail; the precise passenger-service end date for this specific Syracuse-Oswego segment (1935 used here matches the connecting Oswego-Lewiston Hojack Line's own documented end date, not a date sourced for this branch specifically).
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.line: Syracuse, Phoenix and Oswego: Syracuse – Oswego

segments.note: In 1885 George Potts revived part of the abandoned Syracuse Northern Railroad's old Syracuse-Woodard's trackage (see syracuse_northern_railroad.geojson) as the start of a new route, organized as the Syracuse, Phoenix and Oswego Railway and operated as the 'Hojack' branch of the RW&O's St. Lawrence Division. Extended to Phoenix by July 8 1885; 17 miles of new track were built on to Fulton, and the RW&O secured trackage rights from Fulton to Oswego over the New York, Ontario and Western Railway, completing a new 37-mile Syracuse-Oswego route operational by early 1886. Supported through-traffic toward Portland, Maine, and recreational travel to the Three River Point resort along the Fulton segment. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The whole RW&O system, including this Syracuse-Oswego 'Hojack' branch, was leased to the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad effective March 14 1891. At Oswego this route met the other, western half of the Hojack Line proper (Oswego-Sodus-Charlotte-Lewiston, see hojack_line.geojson), whose through passenger service was discontinued February 2 1935 -- used here as a placeholder end date for this connecting branch too, though no source specifically dates this Syracuse-Oswego segment's own passenger-service end. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
